questions.question: Out of the total number of players, 100/3% are in hotel X and the remaining are in hotel Y. If 20 players from hotel Y are shifted to hotel X, then the number of players in hotel X becomes 50% of the total number of players. If 20 players from hotel X are shifted to hotel Y, then the number of players in hotel X becomes what per cent of the total number of players?
questions.questionHtml: Out of the total number of players, 100/3% are in hotel X and the remaining are in hotel Y. If 20 players from hotel Y are shifted to hotel X, then the number of players in hotel X becomes 50% of the total number of players. If 20 players from hotel X are shifted to hotel Y, then the number of players in hotel X becomes what per cent of the total number of players?
questions.solution:
Let total players = A

Players in Hotel X = 100/3% of A = A/3

Players in Hotel Y = A - A/3 = 2A/3

According to question:

A/3 + 20 = 50/100 × A

⇒ A/3 + 20 = A/2

⇒ A/2 - A/3 = 20

⇒ A/6 = 20

⇒ A = 20 × 6

⇒ A = 120

Now, Players in Hostel X = 120/3 = 40 

Players in Hostel Y = 120 - 40 = 80

Now, if 20 players from hotel X are shifted to hotel Y, then the number of players in hotel X becomes,

= 40 - 20 = 20

And the number of players in hotel X becomes what percent of the total number of players:

20/120 × 100

= 16.67%

Hence, ‘16.67%’ is the correct answer.

Hence, ‘112’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: If x + y = 4 and \(\rm \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{16}{15}\) then what is the value of (x 3 + y 3 ) ?
questions.questionHtml: If x + y = 4 and \(\rm \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{16}{15}\) then what is the value of (x3 + y3) ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut TrickWe can use the formula 

(x3 + y3) = (x + y) [(x + y)2 - 3xy]

Given x + y = 4 and \(\rm \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{16}{15}\) 

After solving we get xy = 15/4

Now, From formula, we get 

x3 + y3 = (4) [(4)2 - 3 (15/4)]

x3 + y3 = 4 [16 - 45/4]

x3 + y3 = 4 [19/4] = 19

∴  (x3 + y3) = 19

Alternate Method

Given:

x + y = 4

\(\rm \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{16}{15}\)

Formula used:

(x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy

(x3 + y3) = (x + y)(x2 - xy + y2)

Calculation:

\(\rm \frac{1}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{16}{15}\)

⇒ (y + x)/xy = 16/15 

⇒ 4/xy = 16/15

⇒ xy = 15/4            (1) 

x + y = 4

By squaring both sides.

x2 + y2 + 2xy = 16 

⇒ x2 + y2 = 16 - 2xy 

⇒  x2 + y2 = 16 - 2 × 15/4  

⇒ x2 + y2 = 16 - 15/2 = 17/2       (2)

∵ (x3 + y3) = (x + y)(x2 - xy + y2)

⇒ (x3 + y3) = 4 × (17/2 - 15/4)

∴ (x3 + y3) = 19

Area of ΔABC = 64 cm2

Total CP of 60 fruits = 280 + 360 = Rs. 640.

SP of 12 fruits = Rs. 132 ⇒ SP of 1 fruit = Rs. 11 ⇒ SP of 60 fruits = 11 × 60 = Rs. 660.

Profit % = (20 ÷ 640) × 100 = 3 (1/8)%.

questions.questionHtml: If 8(x + y)<sup>3</sup> - 27(x - y)<sup>3</sup> = (5y - x)(Ax<sup>2</sup> + By<sup>2</sup> + Cxy), then what is the value of (A + B - C) ?
questions.solution:
Given:

8(x + y)3 - 27(x - y)3 = (5y - x)(Ax2 + By2 + Cxy)

Formulas used:

(a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

(a - b)3 = a3 - b3 - 3ab(a - b)

Calculation: 

8(x + y)3 - 27(x - y)3 = (5y - x)(Ax2 + By2 + Cxy)

⇒ 8[x3 + y3 + 3xy(x + y)] - 27[x3 - y3 - 3xy(x - y)] = 5Ax2y + 5By3 + 5Cxy2 - Ax3 - Bxy2 - Cx2y

⇒ - 19x3 + 35y3 + 105x2y - 57xy2 = - Ax3 + 5By3 + 5Ax2y - Cx2y + 5Cxy2 - Bxy2 

By comparing the values of A, B & C in LHS & RHS

⇒ - 19x3 = - Ax3 

∴ A = 19 

⇒ + 35y3 = 5By3

⇒ 35 = 5B 

∴ B = 7

⇒ 105x2y = 5Ax2y - Cx2y

⇒ 105x2y = x2y(5A - C)

⇒ 105 = 5A - C 

⇒ 105 = 5 × 19 - C   [A = 19] 

∴ C = - 10 

Now, (A + B - C) = 19 + 7 - (- 10) 

⇒ 26 + 10 = 36 

∴ The required result = 36

 Alternate Method 

Given 

8(x + y)3 - 27(x - y)3 = (5y - x)(Ax2 + By2 + Cxy)

Concept Used 

a3 - b3 = (a - b)(a2 + b2 + ab)

⇒ [2(x + y)]3 - [3(x - y)]3 = (5y - x)(Ax2 + By2 + Cxy)

⇒ We compare above equation with formula 

So, Ax2 = [2(x + y)]2, By2 = [3(x - y)]2, Cxy = 2(x + y) × 3(x - y)

Now, Let the value of x and y be 1 and -1 respectively 

Then , A = 0 , B = 36 and C =  0

A + B - C = 0 + 36 - 0 = 36

∴ The required answer is 36.

questions.question: If \(\rm \frac{\cos^2 θ}{\cot^2 θ + \sin^2 θ -1} = 3, 0^\circ < θ < 90^\circ\) , then the value of (tan θ + cosec θ) is:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\rm \frac{\cos^2 θ}{\cot^2 θ + \sin^2 θ -1} = 3, 0^\circ < θ < 90^\circ\), then the value of (tan θ + cosec θ) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: cos2 θ / (cot2 θ + sin2 θ − 1) = 3

Using identity sin2 θ − 1 = −cos2 θ, denominator becomes cot2 θ − cos2 θ.

Substituting θ = 60°: cos2 60° = 1/4; cot2 60° = 1/3; sin2 60° = 3/4.

⇒ (1/4) / (1/3 + 3/4 − 1) = (1/4) / (1/12) = 3. Condition satisfied.

Value = tan 60° + cosec 60° = √3 + 2/√3 = (3 + 2)/√3 = 5/√3 = 5√3/3.

∴ The correct answer is 5√3/3.

Alternate Method

Given: cos2 θ / (cot2 θ − cos2 θ) = 3

Formula Used: cot2 θ = cos2 θ / sin2 θ

⇒ cos2 θ / [cos2 θ (1 / sin2 θ − 1)] = 3

⇒ 1 / [(1 − sin2 θ) / sin2 θ] = 3

⇒ sin2 θ / cos2 θ = 3

⇒ tan2 θ = 3 ⇒ tan θ = √3 ⇒ θ = 60°

⇒ tan 60° + cosec 60° = √3 + 2/√3

⇒ (3 + 2) / √3 = 5 / √3 = 5√3 / 3

∴ The correct answer is 5√3/3.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1 and 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ.

Specific Values

For θ = 60°, sin = √3/2, cos = 1/2, tan = √3, and cosec = 2/√3.

Rationalization

To remove a radical from the denominator, multiply the numerator and denominator by the radical: a/√b = (a√b)/b.

questions.questionHtml: Let ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and \(\rm \frac{ar(\Delta ABC)}{ar (\Delta PQR)} = \frac{144}{49}\) If AB = 12 cm, BC = 7 cm and AC = 9 cm, then PR (in cm) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

ΔABC ~ ΔPQR and \(\rm \frac{ar(\Delta ABC)}{ar (\Delta PQR)} = \frac{144}{49}\) 

 AB = 12 cm, BC = 7 cm,  AC = 9 cm

Concept:

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is equal to the ratio of the squares of the corresponding sides.

\(\text{Area of (ΔABC)}\over{\text{Area of (ΔPQR)}}\) = \(({{AC}\over{PR}})^2\)

Calculation:

\(\text{Area of (ΔABC)}\over{\text{Area of (ΔPQR)}}\) = \(({{AC}\over{PR}})^2\) 

⇒ \(144\over49\) = \(({{AC}\over{PR}})^2\) 

⇒ \(AC\over PR\) = \(\sqrt{144\over49} \) = \(12\over7\)

⇒ \(9\over PR\) = \(12\over7\)

⇒ PR = \({9\times 7}\over12\) = \(21\over4\) cm

∴ PR = \(21\over4\) cm

questions.question: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 21% after selling a book at 21% discount on the printed price. The ratio of the cost price and selling price of the book is:
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper earns a profit of 21% after selling a book at 21% discount on the printed price. The ratio of the cost price and selling price of the book is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit % = 21%.

The relation between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) depends on the profit earned.

Multiplier for SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Ratio CP : SP = 100 : (100 + 21) = 100 : 121.

Note: The discount on the printed price is irrelevant for the ratio of CP and SP when profit is given.

∴ The correct answer is 100 : 121.

Alternate Method

Given → Profit % = 21%, Discount % = 21%. Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | Ratio = CP : SP.
⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the book be 100 units. ⇒ Since Profit % = 21%, the Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 21% of 100. ⇒ SP = 100 + 21 = 121 units. ⇒ Ratio of CP : SP = 100 : 121. ∴ The correct answer is 100 : 121.

Additional Information

Relation between CP and MP

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is given by CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%).

Profit and Selling Price

Selling Price is always calculated on Cost Price to determine profit, regardless of the discount offered on the Marked Price.

Speed of the boat going downstream = (Speed of the boat + Speed of the current)

Speed of the boat going upstream = (Speed of the boat - Speed of the current)

Time = Distance/Speed

questions.question: Sides AB and DC of a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD are produced to meet at E and sides AD and BC are produced to meet at F. If ∠ADC = 78° and ∠BEC = 52°, then the measure of ∠AFB is:
questions.questionHtml: Sides AB and DC of a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD are produced to meet at E and sides AD and BC are produced to meet at F. If ∠ADC = 78° and ∠BEC = 52°, then the measure of ∠AFB is:
questions.solution:
Given:

∠ADC = 78° and ∠BEC = 52°

Concept:

The sum of a pair of opposite angles is 180° of a cyclic quadrilateral. 

Calculation:

Now, In quadrilateral ABCD,

∠ADC + ∠ABC = 180° (Sum of opposite angles are 180°)

⇒ ∠ABC = 180° - 78° = 102° 

∠EBC = 180° - 102° = 78° [Linear Pair]

In ΔBEC,

∠BEC + ∠EBC + ∠BCE = 180° 

⇒ 52° + 78° + ∠BCE = 180° 

⇒ ∠BCE = 180° - 130° = 50°

⇒ ∠BCE = ∠DCF = 50° (Vertically opposite angle)

∠ADE + ∠FDC = 180° [Linear Pair]

⇒ ∠FDC = 180° - ∠ADE = 180° - 78° = 102°

In ΔDCF,

∠FDC + ∠DCF + ∠DFC = 180° 

102 + 50 + ∠DFC = 180° 

∠DFC = 180° - 152° = 28° 

∠DFC = ∠AFB = 28° 

∴ The measure of ∠AFB is 28°.

The correct answer is 'The students are being advised by the invigilator not to carry calculators into the examination hall.'

Key Points

  • In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
  • In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
  • The given sentence is in the active voice and it is in the present continuous tense.
  • When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'The invigilator' of the active voice becomes the object, the object 'the students' becomes the subject.
  • The active format "is + V1 (advise) + ing" should be converted into the passive format "are + being + V3 (advised)".
  • This is the active and passive voice rule for the present continuous tense.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Additional Information

  • Verbs of passive format have a different set of tenses (*V3 - Past participle or Third form of the Verb) as given below in the table:
     
    TENSE ACTIVE PASSIVE PASSIVE CONVERSION
    Present Simple He plays football am/is/are + V3 Football is played by him
    Present Continuous He is playing football am/is/are + being +V3 Football is being played by him
    Present Perfect He has played football Has/have + been+ V3 Football has been played by him
    Present Perfect Continuous He has been playing football Not used and unusual. Not used and unusual
    Past Simple He played football Was/were + V3 Football was played by him
    Past Continuous He was playing football Was/were + being + V3 Football was being played by him
    Past Perfect He had played football Had + been + V3 Football had been played by him
    Past Perfect Continuous He had been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Simple He will play football Will + be + V3 Football will be played by him
    Future Continuous He will be playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual
    Future Perfect He will have played football Will have been + V3 Football will have been played by him
    Future Perfect Continuous He will have been playing football Not used and unusual Not used and unusual

 

Hinglish

  • Active Voice में , एक वाक्य विषय पर जोर देता है, एक क्रिया करता है।
  • Passive Voice में , एक वाक्य वाक्य की क्रिया या वस्तु पर जोर देता है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य active voice में है और यह present continuous tense में है।
  • जब हम इस वाक्य को passive voice में बदलते हैं, तो active voice का subject 'The invigilator', object बन जाता है और object 'the students', subject बन जाता है।
  • Active format "is + V1 (advise) + ing" को passive format "are + being + V3 (advised)" में परिवर्तित किया जाना चाहिए।
  • यह present continuous tense के लिए active and passive voice rule है।
     

अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

questions.question: Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. But the eagle, in wrath, gave the beetle a flap of his wing, and straightaway seized upon the hare and devoured him. B. The beetle, therefore, interceded with the eagle, begging of him not to kill the poor suppliant, and pleaded with him not to kill so small an animal. C. When the eagle flew away, the beetle flew after him, to learn where his nest was. D. A hare, being pursued by an eagle, took himself for refuge to the nest of a beetle, whom he begged to save him.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. But the eagle, in wrath, gave the beetle a flap of his wing, and straightaway seized upon the hare and devoured him.

B. The beetle, therefore, interceded with the eagle, begging of him not to kill the poor suppliant, and pleaded with him not to kill so small an animal.

C. When the eagle flew away, the beetle flew after him, to learn where his nest was.

D. A hare, being pursued by an eagle, took himself for refuge to the nest of a beetle, whom he begged to save him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'DBAC'.

Key Points

  • The sentence 'D' is independent of any other sentence as it is giving general information about "a hare". Hence, 'D' is the first part.
  • Sentence B will come after D because it explains how the beetle requested or pleaded with the eagle to not kill the hare.
  • Sentence A will come after B because it explains whether the eagle killed the hare or not.
  • The sentence 'C' is the concluding part because it explains what the beetle has done finally when the eagle flew away.
     

Paragraph after rearranging the sentences: A hare, being pursued by an eagle, took himself for refuge to the nest of a beetle, whom he begged to save him. The beetle, therefore, interceded with the eagle, begging of him not to kill the poor suppliant, and pleaded with him not to kill so small an animal. But the eagle, in wrath, gave the beetle a flap of his wing, and straightaway seized upon the hare and devoured him. When the eagle flew away, the beetle flew after him, to learn where his nest was.

Hint

  • Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles:
    • Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the sentence and eliminate the irrelevant options.
    • Try to identify the opening (independent sentence) and closing sentences (concluding sentence).
    • Try to identify the mandatory pairs. Two sentences can be connected through various connectors and other determinants.
       

Hinglish

  • वाक्य 'D' किसी अन्य वाक्य से स्वतंत्र है क्योंकि यह "एक खरगोश" के बारे में सामान्य जानकारी दे रहा है। अतः 'D' पहला भाग है।
  • वाक्य B, D के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह बताता है कि कैसे भृंग ने बाज से अनुरोध किया कि वह खरगोश को न मारे।
  • वाक्य A, B के बाद आएगा क्योंकि यह बताता है कि बाज ने खरगोश को मारा या नहीं।
  • वाक्य 'C' समापन भाग है क्योंकि यह बताता है कि जब बाज उड़ गया तो बीटल ने आखिरकार क्या किया।

    Direct Speech Indirect Speech

    Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object) Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)

    Past simple (Subject+V2+Object) Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
    Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1+ing+ Object) Past perfect continuous (Subject+had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
    Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object) Present Conditional (Subject+would+V1+object)
    Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object) Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)

 

 

  • दिया गया वाक्य direct speech है।
  • Direct speech को indirect speech में बदलने या बदलने के लिए बुनियादी नियम:

questions.question: Directions: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Had you / not reached in time, / we will have / lost our lives.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Had you / not reached in time, / we will have / lost our lives.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'we will have' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the simple future tense ''will have'' is incorrect.
  • The given sentence is the third conditional sentence explaining that present circumstances would be different if something different had happened in the past.
  • The third conditional sentence format: past perfect, modal auxiliary (would, could, should, etc.)​ + have + past participle.
  • When using the third conditional, we use the past perfect (i.e., had + past participle) in the if-clause and the modal auxiliary (would, could, should, etc.) + have + past participle in the main clause.
  • Therefore, the past form of the verb 'would' should be used in place of the simple future form of the verb 'will'.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: Had you not reached in time, we would have lost our lives.

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में simple future tense ''will have'' का प्रयोग गलत है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य third conditional sentence है जो यह बताता है कि यदि अतीत में कुछ अलग हुआ होता तो वर्तमान परिस्थितियाँ भिन्न होतीं।
  • Third conditional sentence प्रारूप: past perfect, modal auxiliary (would, could, should, etc.)​ + have + past participle.
  • Third conditional का उपयोग करते समय, हम if-क्लॉज में past perfect (i.e., had + past participle) का उपयोग करते हैं और modal auxiliary (would, could, should, etc.) + have + past participle, main clause में।
  • अतः verb 'will' के simple future form के स्थान पर past form of the verb 'would' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
     

अतः सही उत्तर option 4 है।

सही वाक्य: Had you not reached in time, we would have lost our lives.

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है ।
